exact_statement: For every even k>=2 and integer r>=1 on independent uniform physical bits, let G(s,x)=1-2*1{s=0,x=0}, H(s)=(-1)^(sum paired s-coordinate products), A=1{r fresh controls all zero}, Gp=1+A(G-1),Hp=1+A(H-1), and W choose Gp/Hp with one fresh fair selector z. Put a=2^-k,b=2^(-k/2),q=2^-r,c=(1-b+a)/2. All x,shared,selector,activation influences are respectively qa/2,q(a+1/2)/2,qc,qc, and I(W)=q[k/4+(k+1)a/2+(r+1)c]. The exact signed private-query correction D=B_x(W)-B_x(Gp)/2 equals q(2^k-1)S(-a,a;b)+q(1-q)S(-a,a;b-1)+S(1-qa,qa;1-q+qb), S(u,d;v)=[Phi((u+v)^2,d^2)+Phi((u-v)^2,d^2)]/4-Phi(u^2,d^2)/2. For even k>=4 its ratio D/Inf_x(W)>=k-4 and Q_x(W)/Inf_x(W)>=k-11/2 uniformly in r. Taking r=k makes both branch minority probabilities, every root influence and total I(W) tend to zero. Nevertheless an activation-first complete physical policy has B_tree,Q_tree<=5I(W) and H(W)<8I(W). Its activation prefix consumes rqc, has B<=4rqc and retains exactly qH(F), including both terminal core entropies; the surviving base policy consumes qI(F), including final zero-erasure selector influence, at B<=5qI(F). This refutes a universal prescribed-private-query price under rarity/weak-influence hypotheses, not selected-pivot admission or FEI.
